title: Why Redirection Is A Bad Classroom Management Strategy https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2024/02/08/redirection-classroom-management-strategy/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues against the popular classroom management technique of verbal redirection -- quietly or publicly steering a misbehaving student back on task without a formal consequence -- contending it is inconsistent, hard to apply fairly, and ultimately undermines a written classroom management plan's authority. He walks through why redirection tends to be applied unevenly, and how it teaches students that misbehavior can simply be talked away rather than triggering a predictable, promised consequence, eventually turning the teacher into an exhausted, ignored 'micromanager' relying on the same broken-record approach all day. His alternative is straightforward: follow the classroom management plan exactly as written and taught, since a plan's power comes specifically from its unconditional, no-exceptions consistency, something an improvised redirection can never reliably provide.
points: Verbal redirection, though popular, is argued to undermine a classroom management plan because it substitutes an improvised response for a promised, predictable consequence.
Because there's no true accountability, redirection tends to cause more off-task behavior over time, not less, as students learn they can tune it out.
Relying on redirection is described as inevitably turning a teacher into an exhausted, constantly-repeating micromanager by the end of the day.
The recommended alternative is simply following the classroom management plan exactly as written and taught, relying on its unconditional consistency rather than in-the-moment judgment calls.
quotes: Whenever you redirect misbehavior you ignore your classroom management plan. There is no other way to do it. Redirection always replaces what should be a consequence.
You can’t have both a classroom management plan and use redirection. Technically you can, of course, but it will make you by definition inconsistent.
Your students will grow tired of your broken record and eventually just tune you out.
Where there is no accountability and its accompanying reflection, there is no growth.
Only accountability. So what should you do instead? Have a classroom management plan that protects learning and follow it to a tee.
